correctness.rationale: The defining condition is equivalent to every omitted vertex having at most one selected neighbor. For each clique block with omitted parent there can be zero or one selected child vertex; for a selected parent there must be either all omitted children without selected descendants or all selected children. The block messages exactly count these disjoint cases. Vertex messages concatenate independent child blocks while enforcing the omitted-vertex neighbor cap. Tree induction proves arbitrary block graphs; component products and isolated vertices are covered. The windmill formula has a separate direct center/blade proof. From the actual current verifier path, direct subset enumeration agrees coefficientwise on all 8,368 labeled block graphs through order six and 700 clique-glued examples; 562 independent vertex-weight evaluations and 60 windmill profiles also agree. Finite computations are corroboration, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The 2026 initiating counting paper was inspected in full and explicitly handles trees and threshold graphs but not the block-graph clique-incidence recurrence. The highly relevant 2012 block-graph result concerns a different scalar convex-hull Caratheodory number; its complete text was inaccessible, which remains a residual risk. Known bounded-clique-width MSO counting theorems already entail polynomial-time counting on block graphs, so the theorem does not assert novel tractability. The specific positive three-message block-cut formula and full compact multivariate polynomial circuit are not given by the compared prior statements or returned by targeted published-result searches.
residual_risks: A direct three-state recurrence may exist under older block-graph convexity terminology and could be poorly indexed.
The full 2012 block-graph Caratheodory paper was not accessible for page-by-page inspection, so an unadvertised intermediate counting identity cannot be excluded.

General bounded-clique-width MSO counting theory already implies existence of polynomial-time size-weighted counting. The claim is limited to the concrete positive three-state block-incidence arithmetic circuit, not generic tractability.

value.rationale: The 2026 #P-completeness and special-class results motivate explicit transparent counting formulas on other structured graph classes. This theorem gives a natural full multivariate invariant, a constant-three-state positive arithmetic circuit for every clique-block forest including arbitrarily large blocks, all cardinality coefficients, arbitrary nonuniform weights, and a closed clique-bouquet specialization. The exact local case-split and tiny explicit circuit are substantive structural content beyond the generic known bounded-clique-width existence theorem. This is not a textbook substitution nor merely a scalar minimum.
